name: Light Pea Green
lede: Light Pea Green is a vivid yellow-green named for the pea, submitted to the crowdsourced XKCD color survey in 2010 and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a brilliant yellow green.

sections.title: A crowdsourced green
sections.body:
Our data traces the name to the pea, the vegetable, rather than a pigment or a place [1]. It comes from the XKCD color-naming survey of 2010, and the ISCC-NBS system files the same area as block 120, "brilliant yellow green" [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 94, chroma 65, hue 126 degrees: very light and strongly saturated, among the most vivid greens in our data [1].

Two names in the same survey round to almost the same hue: Light Yellow Green, 1.6 units off, and Light Yellowish Green, 1.1 units off, both near-duplicates by our measure [2]. Its nearest distinct neighbor is [[celery|Celery]], 3.0 units off and a little duller, followed by [[light-lime|Light Lime]] [3]. The closest everyday name is [[lime|Lime]], about 8.9 units away [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our 23,781-painting archive has no painting where a close match covers at least one percent of the canvas, as photographed; that describes this archive, not painting as a whole [5]. In printed English the word "light pea green" rose fastest and peaked in the 1930s, across all senses of the phrase, so a color name that is also a plain description of a vegetable can mislead a word count [6].
